This decomposition reflects the global structure of P and provides a foundation for analyzing chain-antichain interactions. The conjecture states that such a decomposition exists with explicitly constructible scattered components that preserve FAC properties.
concept.mathematical_framing: Every countable FAC poset P can be naturally decomposed into a topological sum (ordinal sum) of scattered subposets, where a poset is scattered if it contains no non-trivial dense subposet (i.e., no subset isomorphic to the rationals Q). The conjecture states that such a decomposition exists with explicitly constructible scattered components that preserve FAC properties.
concept.lean_guess: Construct the decomposition by transfinite induction on the construction tree of the FAC poset. Use the fact that countable FAC posets admit a recursive construction from scattered pieces using ordinal sums and certain controlled amalgamation operations. Prove that the resulting components are necessarily scattered by showing that any dense suborder would generate an infinite antichain, contradicting FAC. The proof requires developing machinery to handle the interaction between the chain extension H(P) and the scattered decomposition, leveraging the mutually finite incomparability relation.
